text.p: The following are the stories reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Philip Morris Lietuva's new tobacco factory is expected to start operating in Klaipeda this summer. The factory will produce six billion cigarettes per year.
--Lithuania consumed 30-40 percent less heavy fuel this winter because of the mild weather. The country had 370,000 tonnes of heavy fuel on stock on Friday.
--Though many of the country's commercial banks posted profits for 1996, only Vilniaus, Hermis, Siauliu, Savings, Snoras, Ukio and Tauras are expected to pay dividends.
--After two years of operating in Lithuania, Omnitel has 30,000 subscribers in the country .
--Lithuanian shipping company had a net profit of 55.8 million litas in 1996.
--Estonian experts expect Lithuanian shares to rise sharply this year.

--Nomura does not conceal its interest in participating in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom and says that after the privatisation of the company it will be easier to attract other investors to the country.

--Since the Marijampoles Pieno Konservai, tinned milk producer, was listed on Vilnius bourse its share rocketed by 150 percent. Experts believe that its shares are in demand because it is the only company of its kind in the Baltics. It also plans to expand its production lines and is actively looking for new markets
--Lithuanian insurance companies paid an average of 39.97 percent of their revenues in compensation to their clients in 1996.
